samples.question: The picture shows four rings drawn as flat bands on white paper: one black, one red, one green and one blue. Wherever two bands cross, one of them runs through the crossing unbroken and the other is interrupted by a white gap; the unbroken band is the one passing in FRONT there and the interrupted band passes BEHIND. Every coloured ring crosses the black ring at exactly two places. Call a coloured ring INTERLOCKED with the black ring when the ring in front is different at those two places, that is, the coloured ring is in front at one crossing and behind at the other; if the same ring is in front at both crossings the two rings are NOT interlocked. Crossings between two coloured rings do not matter for this question. Exactly one coloured ring is interlocked with the black ring. Which coloured ring is interlocked with the black ring? Answer red, green or blue.
